concepts.name: Storytelling
concepts.description: Using narrative to make ideas easier to understand, remember, and share.

problems.name: People forget abstract information
problems.description: Important ideas are not remembered because they are too vague, complex, or disconnected from experience.

insights.author: Chip Heath & Dan Heath
insights.chunk_file: outputs/chunks/Made to Stick - Chip and Dan Heath/chunk_001.txt
insights.title: Stories make ideas easier to remember and retell
insights.what_it_says: Stories are easier to understand, remember, and retell than abstract explanations.
how_to_apply: Create a clear sequence of events.
Make the outcome easy to retell.
when_to_use: When explaining an idea people need to remember.
When trying to make information easier to retell.
when_not_to_use: When precision matters more than memorability.
tradeoffs: Stories improve recall but may simplify complex ideas.
insights.evidence: The Kidney Heist is a story that sticks. We understand it, we remember it, and we can retell it later.
